findings.text: Workers always sends Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) parameters.
findings.quote: Workers always sends Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) parameters. The authorization request includes an S256 code challenge, and the token exchange includes the matching code verifier.

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is defined in the worker.oauth configuration.
findings.quote: authorizationEndpoint: "https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize",

findings.text: The token endpoint is defined in the worker.oauth configuration.
findings.quote: tokenEndpoint: "https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token",

findings.text: An empty string for clientSecret will cause the server to reject the request.
findings.quote: An empty string is treated as a configured secret with no value, so the server rejects it.

findings.text: Deploy the worker for the first time.
findings.quote:
1

Deploy your worker

If you haven’t deployed at least once already, do so first. The first deploy registers the worker with Notion.

findings.text: Get the redirect URL for the provider.
findings.quote:
2

Get your redirect URL

ntn workers oauth show-redirect-url

You’ll need this when creating the OAuth app with your provider.

findings.text: Create the OAuth app with the provider.
findings.quote:
3

Create an OAuth app with your provider

Go to your provider’s developer settings (e.g., GitHub Developer Settings, Google Cloud Console) and create an OAuth app. Add the redirect URL from the previous step as an authorized redirect URI.

findings.text: Store the OAuth credentials as secrets.
findings.quote:
4

Store your OAuth credentials

ntn workers env set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=xxx GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=yyy

findings.text: Redeploy the worker to pick up credentials.
findings.quote:
5

Deploy again

Redeploy so the worker picks up the credentials:

ntn workers deploy

findings.text: Start the OAuth flow.
findings.quote:
6

Start the OAuth flow

ntn workers oauth start githubAuth

This opens a browser window where you authorize the connection.

findings.text: You are required to be a workspace owner to create an internal connection.
findings.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

findings.text: Internal connections use a static API token, while public connections use OAuth 2.0.
findings.quote: Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and public connections use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

findings.text: Navigate to the Developer portal and create a new public connection.
findings.quote: Navigate to the Developer portal and create a new public connection.

findings.text: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) and installation scope.
findings.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection’s installation scope — either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only.

findings.text: Direct the prospective user to the authorization URL to start the flow.
findings.quote: To start the authorization flow for a public connection, direct the prospective user to the authorization URL.

findings.text: Exchange the temporary code for an access token by making a POST request to the token endpoint.
findings.quote: Make a POST request to create an access token, which exchanges the temporary code for an access token.

findings.text: Store the access token and refresh token for future API requests.
findings.quote: Store the access token for future API requests.

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize.

findings.text: The token endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.
findings.quote: Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.

findings.text: The supported grant types are authorization_code and refresh_token.
findings.quote: The body of the request contains the following JSON-encoded fields: "grant_type" string Always use "authorization_code".

findings.text: Client authentication uses HTTP Basic Authentication with the client ID and secret.
findings.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET, like so: CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET

findings.quote: If the page is not shared, any API requests made will respond with an error.
